newsitem.title: ITALY: Doctors complete pre-surgery tests on Pope.
newsitem.headline: Doctors complete pre-surgery tests on Pope.

text.p: Doctors preparing Pope John Paul for an operation to remove his appendix completed a battery of tests on the 76-year-old Pontiff on Monday, a senior medical source at Rome's Gemelli hospital said.

The source did not comment on the outcome of the tests, carried out by several specialists. Cardiologist Attilio Maseri, who tested the Pope's heart and blood pressure, said his examinations had shown that "everything is fine".

The Pope was admitted to the Gemelli on Sunday night and is due to have surgery on Tuesday. The Vatican has said recurrent inflammation of his appendix is the cause of three bouts of fever the Pope has suffered since Christmas.
Hospital sources said the pre-surgical examinations included blood and urine tests, an electrocardiogram, an echo-doppler to determine the quality of blood flow and a chest X-ray.
"The Pope is a good patient and also patient with the tests," the senior medical source said. But he added: "I don't think he's very happy to be having these tests. No one likes to be in hospital."

Maseri told reporters that the Pope's blood pressure was "fine" and that other cardiovascular tests he carried out also showed no problems. "Everything is fine. He's okay. He's not (just) "okay with limitations'," Maseri said.
